description: A broad fieldwork questionnaire covering everyday vocabulary and grammatical concepts, including interrogatives.

concepts.definition: The speaker or writer referring to himself or herself alone.
The person addressed.
Third person singular pronoun, regardless of gender/sex.
Inclusive dual of the first person: I and exactly one other person, including the addressed person (you).
Exclusive dual of the first person: I and exactly one other person, but not the addressed person (you).
Inclusive we: I and at least one other person, including the addressed person(s) (pronoun 1st person plural with 2nd person).
Exclusive we: I and at least one other person, but not the addressed person (you) (pronoun 1st person plural without 2nd person).
Addressing two persons (second person dual).
The group of persons addressed.
The third person dual of the personal pronoun.
The third person plural of the personal pronoun that designates more than one person or animal, thing or idea which have already been mentioned previously.
The indicated object, item, etc. close to the speaker.
The indicated object, item, etc. distant from the speaker.
The essential qualities that make a person or a thing distinct from all others.
The rest of a group of.
Belonging to me.
Belonging to the second person that is addressed by the first person.
Belonging to the third person that is addressed.
Belonging to us; of us.
Belonging to the second person that is addressed by the first person, with the second person being many persons and not just one.
Belonging to the third person that is addressed (of many people).
What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).
What person or people; which person or people.
Which thing.
In what way?
For what reason.
At what place?
Directed to what location?
At what time?
The natural number one (1).
Having no predecessor. The ordinal number corresponding to one.
Without any others being included or involved.
The natural number two (2).
That which comes after the first.
The natural number three (3).
The ordinal form of the cardinal number three.
The natural number four (4).
The natural number five (5).
The natural number six (6).
The natural number seven (7).
The natural number eight (8).
The natural number nine (9).
The natural number ten (10).
The natural number eleven (11).
The natural number twelve (12).
The natural number thirteen (13).
The natural number fourteen (14).
The natural number twenty (20).
The natural number twenty-one (21).
The natural number twenty-two (22).
The natural number twenty-three (23).
The natural number twenty-four (24).
The natural number twenty-five (25).
The natural number twenty-six (26).
The natural number twenty-seven (27).
The natural number twenty-eight (28).
The natural number twenty-nine (29).
The natural number thirty (30).
The natural number thirty-one (31).
The natural number forty (40).
The natural number fifty (50).
The natural number sixty (60).
The natural number seventy (70).
The natural number eighty (80).
The natural number ninety (90).
The natural number ninety-nine (99).
The natural number one hundred (100).
The natural number one hundred and one (101).
The natural number one hundred and ten (110).
The natural number one hundred and twenty (120).
The natural number two hundred (200).
The natural number one thousand (1000).
The natural number two thousand (2000).
The natural number ten thousand (10000).
The natural number one hundred thousand (100000).
An unspecified quantity or number of.
The totality of.
Which quantity?
An indefinite large number of.
More than one, but not as many as usual or as expected.
One of the two equal parts of a whole.
More than one, but not as much as usual or as expected. (for mass nouns)
The deity of a monotheistic religion.
The part of the earth's atmosphere and space outside it that is visible from earth's surface. During the day it is perceived as blue, and at night as black.
The Earth with all its inhabitants and all things upon it.
Electromagnetic radiation that is capable of causing a visual sensation. (Source: CED)
The particular star at the centre of our solar system, from which the Earth gets light and heat.
A natural satellite of a planet.
The lunar phase when the moon is fully illuminated by the sun and appears in the sky as a full circle.
The phase in the lunar cycle between new moon and full moon when the illuminated area increases.
The phase in the lunar cycle between full moon and new moon when the illuminated area decreases.
The lunar phase when the moon appears in the sky as a slender crescent shortly after its conjunction with the sun.
A luminous celestial body that is made from gases (particularly hydrogen and helium) and forms the shape of a sphere.
One of the four major compass points, specifically 0°, directed toward the North Pole, and conventionally upwards on a map.
One of the four major compass points, specifically 180°, directed toward the South Pole, and conventionally downwards on a map.
One of the four principal compass points, specifically 90°, conventionally directed to the right on maps. The direction of the rising sun.
One of the four principal compass points, specifically 270°, conventionally directed to the left on maps. The direction of the setting sun.
The dimension of the physical universe which, at a given place, orders the sequence of events.
The period between sunrise and sunset where one enjoys daylight.
The period of time from the start of the day (midnight) until midday (12:00).
Time of day when the sun is in its zenith.
That part of the day in which daylight decreases and the night falls.
The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
Manifestation of collective joy, lasting longer than a few minutes.

Traditionally the second of the four seasons regarded as being from June 21 to September 20 (or just June, July and August) in the Northern Hemisphere and from December 21 to March 20 (or just December, January and February) in the Southern Hemisphere.
The time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
A conflict or a state of hostility between two or more parties, nations or states, in which armed forces or military operations are used.
A state free of war, in particular war between different countries.
The motion of air relative to the earth's surface; usually means horizontal air motion, as distinguished from vertical motion.

An atmospheric disturbance involving perturbations of the prevailing pressure and wind fields on scales ranging from tornadoes to extratropical cyclones; also the associated weather and the like. (Source: MGH)
The violent shaking of the ground produced by deep seismic waves, originating from the epicentre.
Sound produced by fast air expansion induced by a lightning.
The flash of light caused by the discharge of atmospheric electrical charge.
Suspensions of minute water droplets or ice crystals produced by the condensation of water vapour.
Water droplets or, rarely, ice crystals suspended in the air in sufficient concentration to reduce visibility appreciably.
Atmospheric moisture that condenses after a warm day and appears during the night on cool surfaces as small drops.
Precipitation in the form of liquid water drops with diameters greater than 0.5 millimeters.
The soft and loose material forming a great part of the Earth surface.

A specified geographical tract of the Earth's surface including all its attributes, comprising its geology, superficial deposits, topography, hydrology, soils, flora and fauna, together with the results of past and present human activity, to the extent that these attributes exert a significant influence on the present and future land utilization. (Source: WHIT)
A limited area of land with grass or crops growing on it, which is usually surrounded by fences or closely planted bushes when it is part of a farm.
A piece of land next to a house where flowers and other plants are grown and which often has an area of grass.
Level or rolling open land, usually at a low elevation.
A narrow piece of ground that people can walk along.
The non-natural boundary of a region.
The boundary of a surface.
A feature of the earth's surface that rises high above the base and has generally steep slopes and a relatively small summit area.
A vegetation community dominated by trees and other woody shrubs, growing close enough together that the tree tops touch or overlap, creating various degrees of shade on the forest floor.
Areas where the vegetation is dominated by grasses.
A place (commonly marked with a headstone) where one or more people are buried (usually in a coffin underneath the ground).
A, often round, piece of nothingness in some solid.

1) An underground hollow with access from the ground surface or from the sea, often found in limestone areas and on rocky coastlines.2) A natural cavity, chamber or recess which leads beneath the surface of the earth, generally in a horizontal or obliquely inclined direction. It may be in the form of a passage or a gallery, its shape depending in part on the joint pattern or structure of the rock and partly on the type of process involved in its excavation. Thus, caves worn by subterranean rivers may be different in character from, and of considerably greater extent than, a sea-cave eroded by marine waves.3) A natural underground open space, generally with a connection to the surface and large enough for a person to enter. The most common type of cave is formed in a limestone by dissolution. (Source: CED /  WHIT /  BJGEO)
A land mass, especially one smaller than a continent, entirely surrounded by water.
A sandy strip of land close to the sea or ocean.
A general term for rock that is used in construction, either crushed for use as aggregate or cut into shaped blocks as dimension stone.
Any aggregate of minerals that makes up part of the earth's crust. It may be unconsolidated, such as sand, clay, or mud, or consolidated, such as granite, limestone, or coal.
Any kind of solid material divided in particles of very small size.

A loose material consisting of small mineral particles, or rock and mineral particles, distinguishable by the naked eye; grains vary from almost spherical to angular, with a diameter range from 1/16 to 2 millimeters.

A malleable ductile silvery-white ferromagnetic metallic element with symbol Fe and atomic number 26, occurring principally in haematite and magnetite. It is widely used for structural and engineering purposes.
A heavy yellow elemental metal of great value, with atomic number 79 and symbol Au.
A very ductile malleable brilliant greyish-white element with symbol Ar and atomic number 47 having the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal.

Chemical element with symbol Cu and atomic number 29; one of the most important nonferrous metals; a ductile and malleable metal found in various ores and used in industry, engineering, and the arts in both pure and alloyed form.
A crystalline solid, nonmetallic chemical element of a distinct yellow colour, with assigned symbol S and proton number 16.
The state of combustion in which inflammable material burns, producing heat, flames and often smoke.
A bright yellow, red or bluish light which emerges during combustion processes.
A small particle or body of shining or glowing matter, either molten or on fire.
An aerosol, consisting of visible particles and gases, produced by the incomplete burning of carbon-based materials, such as wood and fossil fuels.
The incombustible matter remaining after a substance has been incinerated.
Common liquid (H₂O) which forms rain, rivers, the sea, etc., and which makes up a large part of the bodies of organisms.
A body of salt water that is smaller than an ocean and generally in proximity to a continent.
An enclosed body of water, usually but not necessarily fresh water, from which the sea is excluded.
A stream of water which flows in a channel from high ground to low ground and ultimately to a lake or the sea, except in a desert area where it may dwindle away to nothing.
A hole dug into the earth to reach a supply of water, oil, brine or gas.
A place where ground water flows naturally from a rock or the soil onto the land surface or into a body of surface water.
A muddy and poorly drained area of land, usually near a lake or a river.
A disturbance in an fluid medium.
Area of water next to the coast, often surrounded by thick walls, where ships and boats can be sheltered.
An open, curving indentation made by the sea or a lake into a coastline.

Any living organism that synthesizes its food from inorganic substances, possesses cellulose cell walls, responds slowly and often permanently to a stimulus, lacks specialized sense organs and nervous system, and has no powers of locomotion.
The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
Any large woody perennial plant with a distinct trunk giving rise to branches or leaves at some distance from the ground.
A plant resembling a small tree, but has no, and will never develop, a stem.
The reproductive structure of angiosperm plants, consisting of stamens and carpels surrounded by petals and sepals all borne on the receptacle.
A bud is an undeveloped or embryonic shoot and normally occurs in the axil of a leaf or at the tip of the stem.
The main organ of photosynthesis and transpiration in higher plants, usually consisting of a flat green blade attached to the stem directly or by a stalk.
A flowering plant that is valued for its medical properties.
A botanical fruit that can be eaten raw used as food.
The outer shell or coating of a seed.
The outer layer of fruits.
The wooden shell found inside some fruits, particularly drupes, that surrounds the seed.
The upper part of grain plants.
A woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing.
A branch that doesn't arise from the trunk but from another branch.
The early growth of a plant.
A young plant produced from a seed.
The absorbing and anchoring organ of a vascular plant; it bears neither leaves nor flowers and is usually subterranean.
A bulb is the part of some plants that stores food while the plant is resting from growing.
A sharp and hard structure that grows on a plant.
A mature fertilized plant ovule, consisting of an embryo and its food store surrounded by a protective seed coat (testa).
The exterior covering of the trunk and branches of a tree.
The inner most layer of bark (particularly from a tree).
The juice of plants of any kind, especially the ascending and descending juices or circulating fluid essential to nutrition.
A group of woody perennial evergreen plants in the true grass family Poaceae, subfamily Bambusoideae, tribe Bambuseae.
A vine of the species 'Piper betle' whose leaves are chewed for its medicinal properties.
The fruit of the banana tree.
A species of flowering tree in the mulberry family, Moraceae originating in the South Pacific and that was eventually spread to the rest of Oceania.
The large hard-shelled oval nut with a fibrous husk of the cocos palm.
The fruit of the fig tree, pear-shaped and containing many small seeds.

A very large and widespread family of Monocotyledoneae, with more than 10.000 species, most of which are herbaceous, but a few are woody. The stems are jointed, the long, narrow leaves originating at the nodes. The flowers are inconspicuous, with a much reduced perianth, and are wind-pollinated or cleistogamous.
Cut and dried grass for use as animal fodder.
A tuberous plant, Solanum tuberosum, often eaten as a starchy vegetable, particularly in the Americas and Europe.
A squash fruit of the Cucurbita genus, most commonly orange in colour when ripe and traditionally used during Halloween.
A type of grain of the species Zea mays.
The edible and cultivated fruit of the tree Prunus dulcis in the family Rosaceae. It resembles a nut and can be sold shelled or unshelled.
A spice prepared from the fermented, dried, unripe red berries of the pepper plant.
Any of various types of tall stiff grass-like plants growing together in groups near water.
Starch extracted from the spongy centre, or pith, of various tropical palm stems, especially Metroxylon sagu.
A tropical grass of the genus Saccharum having stout, fibrous, jointed stalks, the sap of which is a source of sugar.

Any living organism characterized by voluntary movement, the possession of cells with noncellulose cell walls and specialized sense organs enabling rapid response to stimuli, and the ingestion of complex organic substances such as plants and other animals.
A large number of animals, especially birds, sheep or goats.
A common, four-legged animal (Sus scrofa) that has cloven hooves, bristles and a nose adapted for digging and is farmed by humans for its meat.
A common four-legged animal, especially kept by people as a pet or to hunt or guard things.
Any of numerous small rodents of the genus ''mus'' or various related genera of the ''Muridæ'' family characterised by a long hairless tail, rounded ears, and a pointed nose.
A nearly omnivorous rodent of the genus ''rattus'' characterised by a long hairless tail, rounded ears, and a pointed nose.

A small, nocturnal, flying mammal of the order Chiroptera, which navigates by means of echolocation. It looks like a mouse with membranous wings extending from the forelimbs to the hind limbs or tail.
Any of the bipedal, warm-blooded vertebrates that lay eggs having wings which, for most species, enables them to fly.
The appendage of an animal's (bird, bat, insect) body that enables it to fly in the air.
A branching, hair-like structure that grows on the skin of birds and protects them against coldness and water and allows their wings to create lift.
Egg (either fertilized or not) from domesticated birds, most commonly hens, seen as food.
A nest in which birds lay and hatch their eggs.
A type of domesticated bird from the order of Galliformes which is often raised as a type of poultry (Gallus gallus domesticus).
A male chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus), a domestic bird.
A young bird that has not yet reached adulthood.
Any bird of the order Psittaciformes, many species of which are colourful and able to mimic human speech.
One of several birds of the family Columbidae.
Any of several large carnivorous birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.
Any reptile of the suborder Serpentes, typically having a scaly cylindrical limbless body, fused eyelids, and a jaw modified for swallowing large prey.
Any large tropical reptile of the family Crocodylidae: order Crocodylia. They have a broad head, tapering snout, massive jaws, and a thick outer covering of bony plates. (Source: CED)

Any reptile of the suborder Lacertilia, especially those of the family Lacertidae, typically having an elongated body, four limbs, and a small tail: includes the gechos, iguanas, chameleons, monitors, and slow worms.

Any insectivorous anuran amphibian of the family Ranidae, such as Rana temporaria of Europe, having a short squat tailless body with a moist smooth skin and very long hind legs specialized for hopping.
Any anuran amphibian of the family Bufonidae, such as Bufo bufo of Europe. They are similar to frogs but are more terrestrial, having a drier warty skin.
A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water that moves with the help of fins and breathes using gills (Pisces).
A scaleless fish with a cartilaginous skeleton that has 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head.
A snake-like edible fish, which lives in freshwater.
One of the small flat pieces of skin that cover the bodies of fish.
An appendage of a fish used for swimming.
Any of the bones forming the skeleton of a fish, especially one of the sharp slender bones attached to the backbone.
A class of the Arthropoda typically having a segmented body with an external chitinous covering, a pair of compound eyes, a pair of antennae, three pairs of mouthparts, and two pairs of wings.
A common insect; any species of insect of the order Diptera.
A fly of the family Tabanidae, known for biting humans.
A small flying insect (of the family Culicidae) known for biting and sucking blood.
Any of the membranous-winged insects which compose the superfamily Apoidea in the order Hymenoptera characterized by a hairy body and by sucking and chewing mouthparts.
A large wasp that can inflict a severe sting, characteristically building large papery nests.
A flying stinging insect related to the bee, which is usually coloured yellow and black.
A lepidopteran that is active at day.
Group of insects related to butterflies.
Any predatory silk-producing arachnid of the order Araneae, having four pairs of legs and a rounded unsegmented body consisting of abdomen and cephalothorax.
Any of the black, red, brown, or yellow insects of the family Formicidae characterized by a large head and by living in organized colonies.
Migratory grasshoppers of the order Orthoptera of warm regions having short antennae.
A group of insects which are biologically classified in the order Coleoptera /koʊliːˈɒptərə/.
A small wingless parasitic insect of the order Phthiraptera that lives on humans, other mammals and birds.
An egg of a louse that is sometimes found in people's hair.
Any of the wingless insects composing the order Siphonaptera; most are ectoparasites of mammals and birds. (Source: MGH)
A small blood-sucking insect that lives in houses, especially beds.
Any of various flattened, wormlike arthropods of the class Chilopoda, whose bodies are divided into many segments, each with one pair of legs.
A generally tubular invertebrate of the annelid phylum.

Decapod crustaceans of the infraorder Brachyura, which typically have a very short projecting tail (abdomen) (Greek: βραχύς / brachys = short, οὐρά / οura = tail), usually entirely hidden under the thorax.
An arthropod with eight legs, belonging to the order Scorpiones in the class Arachnida.
Limestone created from the skeleton of reef-forming stony corals (Scleractinia), displaying their growth patterns.
A class of marine and freshwater molluscs that have laterally compressed bodies enclosed by a shell consisting of two hinged parts.
(Gastropoda) Ventral footed mollusk, including land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusks.
A small hard shiny ball formed in mussels or oysters.
A human being.
An adult human member of the sex that begets young by fertilizing ova.
The male partner in a marriage.
A group of persons forming or belonging to a particular nation, class, ethnic group, country, family, etc.
A group comprising parents, offsprings and others closely related or associated with them.
A person that is considered to be of the same family due to shared ancestors, marriage or adoption.
Person from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any number of generations.
A male parent.
The father of someone's spouse.
A male person who is old of age.
A woman who has at least one child.
The mother of someone's spouse.
Biological offspring.
One's male child.
The male marital partner of someone's child.
A son of someone's child.
A young male person, usually a child or teenager.
A male juvenile between the onset of puberty and maturity; in the state of development between puberty and maturity.
A male person who has the same parents as another person.
A male with more years of age than one or more of his siblings.
A male with fewer years of age than one or more of his siblings.
The brother of one's partner in a marriage.
A female person who has the same parents as another person.
A female with more years of age than one or more of her siblings.
A female who is younger than one or more of her siblings.
The sister of one's partner in a marriage.
An adult human member of the sex that produces ova and bears young.
The female partner in a marriage.
A young female person, usually a child or teenager.
An animal's female offspring (including that of a human).
The female marital partner of someone's child.
A daughter of someone's child.
A woman whose spouse has died.
The brother of someone’s father or mother.
A woman with one or more siblings who have one or more children; a sister of someone's father or mother.
A son of someone's brother or sister.
A daughter of someone’s brother or sister.
A man who is going to get married or has just married.
A woman who is going to get married or has just got married.
A man of noble rank or high office; a nobleman.
A woman of higher social status.
A person who is owned and forced to work, usually without pay, by another.
A person who is owned and forced to work, usually without pay, by another.
Another female partner in a polygamous marriage.
A woman who sells sexual services for money.
The leader/ruler of a tribe/clan.
A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.
A person that visits and stays at a house, usually for one or more nights.
Someone who is hostile to, feels hatred towards, opposes the interests of, or intends injury to someone else.
A person trained in combat or warfare.
The part of the body of an animal or human which contains the brain, mouth and main sense organs.
The back part of the head.
The region of the skull on either side of the forehead.
The main bone of the head; the cranium.
The front part of the head, featuring the eyes, nose, and mouth and the surrounding area.
The hair on humans, usually on the head but also including the hair on the body.
The organ that is sensitive to light, which it converts to electrical signals passed to the brain, by which means animals and humans see.
The partly visible orb nesting in the eye socket which contains for example pupil, retina and iris and is connected to the brain via the optic nerve.
Contractile aperture in iris.
The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
One of the hairs that grows on the eyelid, around the eyes.
The part of the face between the hairline and the eyebrows.
Opening in the lower half of a human face which is used for food ingestion and articulation.
Either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth.
The bottom of the face, below the mouth.
Facial hair of humans on the chin, cheeks and jaw.
Dense, coarse hair that grows on the male and female genital area beginning in puberty.

The flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used to move food around, for tasting and that is moved into various positions to modify the flow of air from the lungs in order to produce different sounds.
A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals (including humans), generally used for eating.
Aeveral teeth located above and below in the mouth of mammals (including humans) to bite food off.
A tooth located in the back of the mouth used for crushing and grinding food.
The soft skin on each side of the face, between the eyes and the chin; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The organ of the face used to breath and smell.
Either of the two orifices located on the nose (or on the beak of a bird); used as a passage for air and other gases to travel the nasal passages.
The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.
The lower fleshy part of the human ear.
The part of the body (found in some animals, including humans) that connects the head and the trunk.
The front part of the neck.
The back part of the neck.
A lump at the front of the neck.
The physical structure of a human or animal.
The central part of the human body, from which neck and limbs extend.
A dead body.
The portion of the body from the base of the neck to the top of the abdomen; the thorax.
The fleshy organ on the chest of a sexually mature human female containing mammary glands.
An organ in female quadruped mammals which consists of mammary glands and has several teats.
The projection of a mammary gland from which, on female mammals, milk can be secreted.
The lower part of the front of the torso (or a comparable part of an animal), confined by the upper side by the midriff and the lowerside by the pelvis. Contains the intestines.
A scar where the umbilical cord was attached.
A conduit between the developing embryo or fetus and the placenta.
One side of the top of the torso, where an arm attaches or joins.
The hollow under the upper part of the arm at the shoulder.
The rear of body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and belly.
The fleshy part of the human body that one sits on.
The lower opening of the digestive tract, through which faeces pass.
The appendage of an animal that is attached to its posterior and near the anus.
The male sexual organ for copulation and urination; the tubular portion of the male genitalia (excluding the scrotum).
The male sex gland that produces sperm and male hormones, found in some types of animals and humans.
Anatomical male reproductive structure.
The external parts of the female genitalia, in human beings this consists of the labia, clitoris, opening of the urethra (meatus), and the opening of the vagina.
The lower part of the female reproductive tract; a moist canal in female mammals (including humans) extending from the labia minora to the uterus.
A part of the female genitalia located at the front of the vulva, consisting of a sensitive erectile body.
The upper limb, extending from the shoulder to the wrist and sometimes including the hand.
The part of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow.
The part of the arm between the elbow and the hand.
The joint between arm and forearm.
That part of the fore limb below the forearm or wrist in primates (including humans).
The inner and somewhat concave part of the human hand that extends from the wrist to the bases of the fingers.
The flexible and narrower connection between the forearm and the hand.
The closed hand with the fingers on the palm.
One of the long extremities of the hand that is used for gripping objects.
The shortest and thickest of the fingers that can be placed against the others in order to create a firm grip.
One of the extremities of the foot.
Hard keratin part growing at the end of a human's finger or toe.
The hard, keratin part growing at the feet of animals.
Natural horn covering of an animal's foot.
The limb of an animal (including humans) that extends from the groin to the ankle.
The part of a human’s body below the ankle that is used in order to stand and walk.
The arched part of the human foot between the ankle and the toes.
The bottom of the foot.
A joint formed where the foot and the leg meet.
The outward-projecting parts of the pelvis and top of the femur and the overlying tissue.
The part of the leg between the pelvis and the knee.
Part of the leg between the knee and the foot.
The front part of the leg below the knee.
In man, the joint in the middle part of the leg.
The fleshy backside of the lower part of the leg.
The part of the human foot on the backside where it becomes the leg.

The tissue forming the outer covering of the vertebrate body: it consists of two layers, the outermost of which may be covered with hair, scales, feathers, etc. It is mainly protective and sensory in function.
The body-hair of an animal (excluding humans) or a piece of clothing made thereof.
Any of the components of an endoskeleton, consisting mainly of calcium phosphate, collagen and cells.
One of the long curved bones which form the rib cage.
Bone linking the scapula and sternum.
Either referring to the soft substance of the body of living things (flesh), or to the soft substance in animals as an important source of food for humans.
Tissue that connects muscle to bone.
The blood vessels are the part of the circulatory system that transports blood throughout the human body or an animal body.
The rhytmic contraction and expansion of arteries at each heart beat, often discernible at points such the wrists and the neck.
A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body.
A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. Responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
An organ in the body that produces urine.
A ductless vascular gland, located in the left upper abdomen near the stomach.
A biological organ that extracts oxygen from the air.
An organ in the body, involved in digestion of food.
A hollow muscular balloon-shaped organ that stores urine until it is excreted from the body.
The alimentary canal of an animal or human through which food passes after having passed all stomachs.
A fluid connective tissue consisting of the plasma and cells that circulate in the blood vessels.
The whitish fluid secreted by the mammary gland for the nourishment of the young; composed of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, mineral salts, vitamins, and antibodies.
A fluid that is secreted by sweat glands in the skin in order to regulate body temperature.
